title: step_test_command_observation_persistence holds StateInner for up to 4.5 s: the day's top lock hold (test_run_observations.rs:880)
outcome: The idle test-command observation persistence step no longer holds StateInner for seconds. Expensive work (scanning unclassified commands against session runtime identities, compaction and persistence preparation) runs on a snapshot or outside the lock, with the same results.
acceptance: A cause note names the expensive operations held under the lock in step_test_command_observation_persistence (test_run_observations.rs:879 onward) with file:line, based on reading the code at the running master. It's labelled as a reading, not a profile, per Greg's direction to fix from code first.

The observation-persistence step no longer scans or clones a backlog-sized collection, performs a backlog-by-sessions lookup, polls persistence waiters, or builds a full-history projection while holding StateInner. Candidate discovery and coherent input capture use bounded resumable batches owned by the existing collections; per-acquisition work is bounded by the batch and affected identities, with no hidden full scan in cursor advancement or session lookup. Runtime identity formatting/hashing and candidate computation run off-lock. Application revalidates each exact current entry, session/runtime and persistence fence before changing state, batches changed rows through the existing persistence owner, uses targeted publication and defers compaction. Under a quiescent finite backlog, repeated steps eventually examine every eligible entry; concurrent insertion, replacement and removal cannot lose work or apply a stale result. Tests with large unrelated history and many sessions establish bounded scan/capture work and unchanged durability, failure and publication semantics. The existing disconnected synchronous persistence fallback keeps its ordering; it is explicitly outside this scan/capture complexity claim and is not represented as bounded or moved off-lock without an existing owner protocol.
The review pair has no outstanding Medium-or-higher finding, and the full gate passes on the exact committed tree.
